info.title: HALO B05 discovery backend contract
info.description: The six operations B05 built or fixed: map.layer and map.district (the two shipped map routes, fixed for quarter=latest and an incomplete geography lookup), locations.search, explore.area.read, explore.area.save and map.comparison. Dropped, and absent here: community.read and map.brief (no consumer, validator or type on the frontend ref). Blocked, and absent here: organizations.search (no participation content) and summary.prepare, summary.list and summary.read (no record collections to freeze). Response schemas mirror the frontend's own validators and parsers on origin/codex/october15-review-refinement (explore-service.ts, map-service.ts), which discard or refuse the whole payload on one wrong field; where a rule is not JSON Schema the conformance test transcribes the validator instead. Only statuses each handler can produce are listed. Every body is bare: none carries a top-level data key (Ruling D10). The three map operations are public (B05 Task 6, approved by Vibhav on 2026-10-19): a request with no Authorization header at all is an anonymous, cache-only read, limited to 60 requests a minute per visitor and shared-cacheable for 10 minutes; any Authorization header is checked exactly as before. The other three operations require a session. Nothing here is a deployment or approval claim beyond this one: migration 0022, which explore.area needs, was applied to production on 2026-10-19. Version b05-2 covers two changes, neither shipped before it: the three map operations became public (B05 Task 6), and DiscoveryPlace was widened from counties to North Carolina's Census places and ZCTAs, so its id now also admits us-place and us-zcta (B05 Task 8). A consumer that read b05-1 must accept both.

get.summary: One map layer: water, radon, facilities or air
get.description: Served from the daily pre-build (map_layers, migration 0011); a missing or stale layer is built live and, when complete, stored. Public read (B05 Task 6, lib/publicAccess.js): a request with no Authorization header at all is anonymous; any Authorization header, however malformed, is checked as before and is a 401 when it is not a valid session, never downgraded. An anonymous request is cache-only: it is answered only from what is already stored and never builds, stores or makes an outbound call; with nothing stored it is a 503. It is limited to 60 requests a minute per visitor across the three map routes, keyed by a digest of the forwarded client address, and the limiter fails open. A successful anonymous answer carries Cache-Control public, max-age=0, s-maxage=600; every other answer from the three map routes is private, no-store. All of them send Vary: Authorization. Anonymously, a layer is answered only from the stored pre-build, and a water quarter only when the service-area geography is already in the cache (a cache miss is never answered as a layer with every system unlocated). A water quarter is assembled from the UCMR 5 table for the time slider and is never stored. A live water build whose service-area lookup did not complete is still answered, marked geography_complete false and meta.availability partial with a note that says so, and is not stored; the client reads meta.availability partial as an incomplete layer (map-service.ts:31). The body is bare: no top-level data key (Ruling D10), because the client would parse body.data instead.

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: Default water. district is served by /api/district and is a 400 here.

parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: latest, or a sampling quarter YYYYQn. latest (exactly, lowercase) means no quarter on every layer, exactly like an omitted or empty parameter, and is checked first (B05 Ruling D2, lib/mapQuarter.js). A YYYYQn on a layer other than water is a 400 quarter_not_applicable; anything else on water is a 400 invalid_quarter. Latest and LATEST are not latest. Applicability is checked before format, so a malformed quarter on a non-water layer is quarter_not_applicable.

get.summary: NC-08's water picture from public data, with the caller's own county
get.description: The stored district view (map_layers, district) or a live build, plus household_county: the caller's county in the statewide ranking, read from their own profile. The full statewide ranking (county_rankings) stays server side and is forbidden here. With no stored view and a service-area lookup that did not complete, the answer is a 503 and nothing is stored: every count is a required integer, so a partial placement would read as 0 systems with a complete population. Contradiction 9.9 (the no-population branch the client rejects) is unreachable through every producer and pinned by test, so every by_contaminant row carries population_over and over_population_unknown. Public read (B05 Task 6, lib/publicAccess.js): a request with no Authorization header at all is anonymous; any Authorization header, however malformed, is checked as before and is a 401 when it is not a valid session, never downgraded. An anonymous request is cache-only: it is answered only from what is already stored and never builds, stores or makes an outbound call; with nothing stored it is a 503. It is limited to 60 requests a minute per visitor across the three map routes, keyed by a digest of the forwarded client address, and the limiter fails open. A successful anonymous answer carries Cache-Control public, max-age=0, s-maxage=600; every other answer from the three map routes is private, no-store. All of them send Vary: Authorization. Anonymously, only the stored view is answered, no profile is read, and household_county is absent (not null, which would say the county is not ranked). Bare body (Ruling D10).

get.summary: North Carolina counties, cities and towns, and ZIP codes a household can choose as its Explore area
get.description: Licence-free public-domain Census gazetteers in the repo (B05 Ruling D4, widened by Task 8): the TIGERweb county set, the 2026 Gazetteer places (cities, towns, villages and census-designated places) and the 2020 ZCTAs with land in North Carolina. No table is read and no provider is called. Matching ignores case, whitespace and punctuation; a county also matches without a trailing County or Co., and after that word the county leads, while a place still matches the whole query exactly or by prefix (Yadkin Co is Yadkin County, then Yadkin College; Columbus County is the county only, since no place starts with it). Every exact match comes before every prefix match, and within each counties come before places, each by name, so "Wake" is Wake County then Wake Forest. A query of two or more characters also matches the start of a name. A query of digits, optionally after ZIP, is a ZIP code: five digits are one exact ZCTA, three or four digits the ZCTAs they start, ZCTAs in numeric order. A ZIP is a ZCTA, so a PO-box or unique ZIP with no ZCTA, such as 27699, finds nothing. Mt and Mount, St and Saint, and Ft and Fort are one word (Mt Airy is Mount Airy, Saint Pauls is St. Pauls). When the query names no NC area exactly and ends, after at least one other word, in NC, N.C. or North Carolina, with or without a comma (Charlotte, NC; Charlotte NC; Charlotte N.C.; Raleigh, North Carolina), the words before it are searched. Any other state counts only when a comma sets it off (Raleigh, VA; Charlotte, Hawaii), and gives no candidates. Without a comma the last word stays part of the name, so a word being typed still matches by prefix (Chapel Hi is Chapel Hill, Washington Pa is Washington Park). Co is the county word, never Colorado. At most 20 candidates, a cap short queries such as "Ca" or "282" reach. So the chooser's examples, "Charlotte" and "28208", each answer one candidate. A non-NC state, or an unknown name or ZIP, is a 200 with no candidates, which the client shows as no matching area; the body cannot say "unsupported geography" (finding F3). Bare body (Ruling D10).

patch.summary: Save or clear the household's discovery area
patch.description: The body is exactly { place, revision }; anything else is refused. Only place.id is read: it is resolved against the county, place and ZCTA gazetteers (lib/places.js placeById) and the gazetteer's own five fields are stored and returned (Ruling D8), so an unknown id is a 400 and a forged label never reaches the database. Idempotency is the operation ledger (domain explore, kind explore.area.save): the Idempotency-Key header is required, the precondition is checked inside the operation so a replay gets the first outcome, and the ledger input is { place, revision } as sent. Every refusal is a 409 the client maps to a conflict, which clears its parked operation; the reason says why (see the 409). A pending attempt inside the ledger's window is the one replay whose outcome is honestly unknown, the retryable 503 upstream_unavailable; settling a stale one depends on the reaper. Migration 0022 was applied to production on 2026-10-19.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: The client's own operation id, a UUID, stable across a replay. Missing, empty or not a UUID is a 400 naming Idempotency-Key. The id is never put in the body.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The revision the client holds, the same number as the body's revision (runtime.ts:133). Different, or quoted, is a 400 precondition_mismatch on field revision: a client sending two preconditions does not know what it is asking for. The revision a save returns is accepted as the next If-Match.

409.description: A terminal refusal, with reason: stale_revision (the area moved on; revision is the current one), revision_exhausted (the area is at 2147483647 and cannot take another revision; revision is that value), operation_mismatch (this Idempotency-Key was already used with a different body, or by another household), or, on a replay of an earlier attempt that is over without a receipt, abandoned (the ledger reaped it because it never settled within its window) or attempt_failed (it threw inside the operation, or its stored reason is one this route never writes). The last two compared no revision, so they are never called stale.

get.summary: The public records the comparison sheet sets side by side, honestly degraded
get.description: Every record carries no method, no source version, every value qualifier unknown and coverage partial (B05 Ruling D3), so the client's compareEvidence answers "Not comparable" with the method, source and qualifier reasons for every pair and nothing can render "Aligned evidence" or "Limited comparison". That is a statement about the data HALO holds, not a defect: the only route to alignment is acquiring UCMR 5 method, release and non-detect qualifiers (tracker HO-074; open question 3). No sourceName is sent (the client falls back to "Source not reported"). Sources: water latest from the stored water layer, else the UCMR 5 table with no geography lookup; a water quarter from the UCMR 5 table; air from the stored air layer only, else a 503 (so while /api/map answers a live air build the comparison can still be blocked); facilities and radon have no comparable observation and answer no records with nothing read. No outbound call and no household table. Public read (B05 Task 6, lib/publicAccess.js): a request with no Authorization header at all is anonymous; any Authorization header, however malformed, is checked as before and is a 401 when it is not a valid session, never downgraded. An anonymous request is cache-only: it is answered only from what is already stored and never builds, stores or makes an outbound call; with nothing stored it is a 503. It is limited to 60 requests a minute per visitor across the three map routes, keyed by a digest of the forwarded client address, and the limiter fails open. A successful anonymous answer carries Cache-Control public, max-age=0, s-maxage=600; every other answer from the three map routes is private, no-store. All of them send Vary: Authorization. Every source here is already cache-only, so an anonymous request gets the signed-in body. Bare body (Ruling D10).

SafeText.description: The frontend's text() predicate (explore-service.ts:9) without its max: a string free of U+0000 to U+0008, U+000B, U+000C and U+000E to U+001F. Tab, line feed and carriage return are permitted. Compose it with maxLength through allOf.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The shared HALO error envelope (lib/apiErrors.js). The client reads none of it: runtime.ts:144 maps the status to a failure code and shows its own sentence. Strict here, because a field that leaked a database message or another household's id would leak it into a log.

error.description: The legacy sentence; equal to message.

MapErrorEnvelope.description: The envelope, plus the legacy layer field on GET /api/map's upstream 503 (the auth outage carries none).

error.description: The legacy sentence; equal to message.

ConflictEnvelope.description: A 409 from PATCH /api/explore/area. code is always conflict and retryable false. revision is present exactly when the reason is about the stored revision.

error.description: The legacy sentence; equal to message.

DiscoveryPlace.description: The frontend's DiscoveryPlace (explore-service.ts:66-67): five strings of at most 300 SafeText characters, id non-empty. The id pattern, the state and the timezone are statements about THIS release, which serves North Carolina only (Ruling D4): its 100 counties, its Census places (cities, towns, villages and census-designated places) and its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (B05 Task 8, open question 2 answered by Vibhav on 2026-10-19). Any other geography is a new contract version.

id.description: us-county:<GEOID> (a five-digit NC county GEOID), us-place:<GEOID> (a seven-digit NC Census place GEOID) or us-zcta:<ZCTA5> (a five-digit NC ZCTA, 27xxx or 28xxx)

place.description: <Name> County for a county, <Name> for a place (the Census name less its city, town, village or CDP word; two places of one name carry their county in parentheses), <ZCTA5> for a ZIP code

label.description: <Name> County, NC; <Name>, NC; or ZIP <ZCTA5>, NC

LocationCandidates.description: validPlaces (explore-service.ts:67): at most 20 candidates. An empty list is an answer, not an error.

DiscoveryArea.description: validDiscoveryArea (explore-service.ts:69). revision is a safe integer above 0 (the database ceiling is 2147483647); place is a DiscoveryPlace or null. pendingOperation, which the frontend type permits, is forbidden in this release (Ruling D7).

ExploreAreaSave.description: Exactly the two fields the client sends (ExploreDiscovery.tsx:60). place is null to clear, or a place whose id is read and nothing else (Ruling D8). revision is a JSON number, never a string.

WaterCompound.description: One regulated compound for one system. Tested: value_ppt, ratio, date and date_iso are present. Not tested: severity no_data and only the limit, never a zero.

HazardIndex.description: The latest-sample PFAS hazard index, present only when two or more of its compounds were detected. A latest-sample value, not a compliance determination.

WaterFeature.description: One public water system. lat, lng and population are joined by PWSID from the service-area lookup and are null when it has none (or did not finish).

MapLayerWater.description: The water layer, statewide; counts describe exactly the features returned. geography_complete false and meta.availability partial appear together, and only on a live build whose service-area lookup did not complete; such a body is never stored.

MapLayer.description: One of the four layers, told apart by layer. The client's parseMapLayer (map-service.ts:24-56) throws on a layer other than the one asked for or a features value that is not an array.

MapDistrict.description: parseMapDistrict (map-service.ts:82-96) requires every count as a non-negative integer and throws otherwise, so every counter is required here. county_rankings (the statewide ranking) is deliberately not a property: it stays server side.

MapDistrictPublic.description: The anonymous district answer (B05 Task 6): the stored view exactly as MapDistrict, with no household_county property at all, because there is no household. parseMapDistrict does not read household_county, so the client parses both.

MapDistrictAnswer.description: The 200 of map.district: MapDistrict for a signed-in household (with household_county), MapDistrictPublic for an anonymous request (without it).

ComparisonValue.description: One observation. method null and qualifier unknown are fixed by Ruling D3: HALO holds no analytical method and no non-detect qualifier, and composing either would be a false provenance claim. value is null when nothing was reported, never 0.

ComparisonRecord.description: One public record for the comparison sheet (parseMapComparisons, map-service.ts:58-65). sourceVersion and sourceUrl null, status available and coverage partial (never complete) are fixed by Ruling D3. No sourceName.
